intro: One row per system of the base game: what state AmiWind has it in, which reference decides how it should behave, where the proof is, and which work items and register entries carry the rest. The states are taken from the work lists and the bug register; a row is marked done only when it names a proof.

mwscript.source: tools/mwscript/functions.py (the compiler's own table, counted in the builder container on 9 November 2026) and the builder's script measurement (docs/MWSCRIPT_BYTECODE.md)
mwscript.scripts_measured: 9 November 2026, v0.0.63; 9 more are carried by the game's own code
mwscript.note: used_and_carried_out is pending: the builder's script report does not record the used functions per build, so the overlap of the 251 used with the 460 carried out needs one run of python3 -m mwscript.measure on the game data in the builder container (MWSCRIPT-MORE-57). By master: Morrowind.esm 616 scripts = 518 run, 9 carried by the game's own code, 1 only in an add-on world, 88 that nothing in the original names or starts, so every Vvardenfell script the original uses runs; Tribunal.esm 255 = 42 run in Vvardenfell, 8 lack a function, 186 wait for Mournhold, 19 not used; Bloodmoon.esm 336 = 45 run, 20 lack a function, 245 wait for Solstheim, 26 not used.

features.name: Vvardenfell exteriors
features.what: Every exterior cell of the base game as terrain, water, objects and sky on the CHIM world, streamed as the player walks.
features.reference: OpenMW 0.51 cell and terrain loading; UESP Morrowind:Vvardenfell
features.proof: docs/chim/CELL_TRACKER.md (1,390 of 1,390 cells converted and audited); tests/aga_chim_world_test.c, tests/test_world_survey.py.

features.name: Interiors
features.what: Every interior of the base game but two as CHIM rooms with their lights, doors and residents; the load doors link both ways. Every room's containers, items and creatures are counted against the original; since v0.0.63 a container in a room is aimed at by its placement box, and an item can be dropped on an uneven tomb or cave floor (seen in the Andrano Ancestral Tomb on v0.0.63-dev3).
features.reference: OpenMW 0.51 cell loading; UESP Morrowind:Interior cells
features.proof: tests/test_chim_rooms.py, tests/aga_chim_room_record_test.c, tests/test_world_ledger.py; release notes of v0.0.50 (every entrance linked both ways) and v0.0.63-dev2 (the room census).
features.missing: Two interiors are not converted; 110 items of 82 rooms are not drawn; the aim at containers in rooms is not yet seen in play; the items, containers and creatures of rooms are not yet loaded from per-area tables.

features.name: Tribunal and Bloodmoon
features.what: The two expansions' cells, quests and creatures. The builder reports at the end of the game-file check whether each expansion's files were found and what of each it uses (v0.0.63-dev5); Tribunal and Bloodmoon creatures are built, and the scripts that sit in Vvardenfell run (Tribunal 42 of 255, Bloodmoon 45 of 336).
features.reference: OpenMW 0.51 content loading; UESP Tribunal and Bloodmoon pages
features.missing: Mournhold and Solstheim are not in the image: 186 Tribunal scripts and 245 Bloodmoon scripts wait for them, and no quest of the expansions can run.

features.name: Doors and load doors
features.what: Hinged doors open and close, load doors move the player between cells with the destination marker, locks follow the game data and the scripts.
features.reference: OpenMW 0.51 door and teleport handling; UESP Morrowind:Doors
features.missing: Gates, trapdoors, hatches and bar counter flaps do not move; load doors into rooms read no lock until lockpicks and keys exist.

features.name: Travel services
features.what: Silt strider, boat, gondola and guild guide travel from the travel provider's dialogue, with the fare and the arrival place.

features.name: Weather
features.what: Weather states, their sky and fog, and the choice by region.
features.reference: OpenMW 0.51 weather and region records; UESP Morrowind:Weather
features.missing: Ash storms and blight storms in their regions are not driven by the region records yet.

features.name: Day, night and sky
features.what: The calendar clock, sun and moons, the night sky, window and lamp lighting at night.
features.reference: OpenMW 0.51 sky and time of day

features.name: Water and lava
features.what: Swimming, the sea, and lava that hurts. Since v0.0.63 the player holds his breath for the original's time under water, a breath bar shows, and when it runs out he takes the drowning damage; Water Breathing from race abilities, potions, spells and worn items lets him breathe.
features.reference: OpenMW 0.51 water, breath and lava handling
features.missing: Breath and drowning are checked by tests but not yet seen to work in play: an Argonian's Water Breathing failed the v0.0.63-dev3 check and was fixed in v0.0.63-dev4; the water level cannot be changed by scripts (the water is baked).

features.name: Placed objects
features.what: The statics, flora, lights and loose items the original places, drawn from one model table. Since v0.0.63 fire pits burn, scripts move and turn the world objects they name (the Ghostgate portcullises), and moved or turned objects are kept in saved games.
features.reference: OpenMW 0.51 reference placement; the original's cell records
features.missing: Not every placed item is drawn and takeable from the shared model table yet; trees have no depth steps; the burning fire pits and the moved world objects are checked by tests, not yet seen in play.

features.name: Area sounds
features.what: The looping sounds of the invisible sound markers.
features.reference: OpenMW 0.51 sound markers (static sounds); UESP Morrowind:Sound
features.missing: The sound markers are not played: no looping area sounds yet.

features.name: Residents in the world
features.what: Characters stand where the original places them, with the right face, hair and gear, in the exteriors and rooms that are built.
features.missing: Bodies are still baked into the image rather than built from parts at run time; the recipe tables are being cut per area.

features.name: Wander, idle and travel
features.what: Residents walk and idle on their records' packages, and the scripts can send them travelling. Characters fight each other when a script sets them against each other, and allies and guards join a fight (v0.0.63).
features.reference: OpenMW 0.51 behaviour packages (wander, travel); UESP Morrowind:NPCs
features.missing: Schedules by time of day, escort and the other packages are not carried out; compiled wander packages are built but off by default.

features.name: Creatures
features.what: Creatures on their own models with idle, wander, walk, run and attack on sight. Since v0.0.63 walking creatures stand on the ground, hostile ones attack on their own indoors and out (the ancestor ghost of the Andrano Ancestral Tomb was seen attacking on v0.0.63-dev3), and creatures met late in a long outdoor session walk, run and attack instead of gliding on idle frames; the cliff racer's strikes land in the open world.
features.proof: tests/test_creature_tables.py, tests/aga_chim_actor_table_test.c, tests/test_actor_anim_reach.py (every creature whose original has walk, run or attack groups reaches them).
features.missing: Outdoor creatures walking and attacking (an ash slave, a corprus stalker), the cliff racer's drawn size, the fish and the pack behaviour are not yet seen in play; Dagoth Ur's fight and voice are not in.

features.name: Followers and companions
features.what: A follower keeps with the player inside a cell and, since v0.0.62, goes through doors, travel and region loads with the player; an escort leads the player to its destination (AIFollowCell, AIEscort, AIEscortCell). Since v0.0.63 followers side with the player in a fight, and the followers and escorts of the scripts move by the same follow behaviour as the companion test mode.
features.missing: Going through doors and a follower's fight beside the player are not yet seen in game; a follower whose home is outdoors comes back after a saved game is loaded only once its home area is loaded.

features.name: Animation
features.what: Standing, walking, running, fighting and scripted animation groups on skeletal actors; creatures get their walk, run and attack groups for the whole outdoor session (v0.0.63-dev3).
features.reference: OpenMW 0.51 animation groups; the original's keyframe files
features.missing: Not every character plays its full set of sequences; the third-person casting gesture and the attack types are not drawn; walk and run cycles are being made cheaper.

features.name: Spawning by script
features.what: Characters, creatures and items placed by scripts through one shared spawn. Since v0.0.62 the scripts' PlaceAtPC, PlaceAtMe, PlaceItem and PlaceItemCell make an NPC or creature whose record the world places somewhere (spawned from that reference's entity, kept on the world change list) and any carried item (a drop row).
features.proof: tests/aga_spawn_test.c, tests/test_entity_spawn_contract.py, tests/test_mwscript.py (the placing family); docs/MWSCRIPT_BYTECODE.md (placing objects).
features.missing: Spawned references are not yet proven across a save and reload in game. Records no reference places (no converted model) and activators, containers and levelled lists are not placed yet.

features.name: Character creation
features.what: The Census Office questions, race, face, hair, class and birthsign, with the install's class questions. The opening from the prison ship to the census office is AmiWind's own code; since v0.0.63 it starts with the original's state (the character generation state, the ship guard's steps, the captain's hint, the cloudy Bitter Coast weather, the dock guard at his post), compared step by step with the eight scripts it carries.
features.reference: OpenMW 0.51 character generation; UESP Morrowind:Character Creation
features.proof: tests/test_chargen_questions.py, tests/aga_quickchar_test.c, tests/aga_chargen_class_review_test.c, tests/test_mwscript_counterparts.py; docs/MWSCRIPT_FEATURES.md (the eight scripts and their parity).
features.missing: The opening's changes of v0.0.63 are checked by tests, not yet seen in play.

features.name: The player's body and gear
features.what: The player's hands and body in first and third person, assembled from parts by what is worn: armour and clothes, the drawn weapon and shield, a held light, the sleeves in the first-person view, and the swimmer's own clothes.
features.reference: OpenMW 0.51 first and third person; the original's body parts
features.missing: Gauntlets on the first-person hands and a still of every worn piece are not yet seen in game; a held lantern hangs below the hand, and the held light is not in the inventory picture.

features.name: Player movement
features.what: Walking, running, jumping, swimming, steps and collision on the original's movement rules.

features.name: Attributes and skills
features.what: The stat sheet with attributes, skills, health, magicka and fatigue, and the race and class numbers.
features.proof: tests/aga_statswin_test.c, tests/test_race_stats.py, docs/ACTOR_RECORDS.md (the index of every value a being can hold), docs/GAME_FORMULAS.md (every calculation and its status).
features.missing: The stat window, levelling, rest and the combat sheets still read their own copies instead of the one set of stats every being now carries (docs/ACTOR_STATS.md).

features.name: Levelling
features.what: The level-up rules and the attribute multipliers.
features.proof: tests/aga_levelup_rules_test.c, tests/test_levelup.py (the rules); the level-up box after a rest was seen in game on v0.0.61-dev1.
features.missing: Skills trained at a trainer do not yet count toward the level.

features.name: Rest and wait
features.what: The rest rules and the wait dialog.
features.reference: OpenMW 0.51 rest and wait; UESP Morrowind:Resting
features.missing: Resting heals and levels up and waiting only passes time, both refused near enemies: the in-game behaviour is not yet proven end to end.

features.name: Saved games
features.what: Saves keep the character, the position, equipment, the journal, topics and the changes made to actors and objects.
features.missing: Taken objects, doors and locks, script variables and the calendar are not all kept (moved and turned world objects, the werewolf form, the forced run and the water breathing are); no default save titles; no import of the original's saves.

features.name: Weapons
features.what: Melee swings and the hit rules against actors, with the weapon kit; weapons and shields of every type drawn in their stance in both views, the two-handed rules, two first-person sway styles, creatures that resist normal weapons, god mode that holds back every damage. Since v0.0.63: the always use best attack option (Options and console, one saved value, on by default), the chance to hit with Fortify Attack, Blind, Sanctuary, Chameleon and Invisibility, a blow that reaches the nearest fighter in the original's hit cone with the opponent's health bar, and fights between characters.
features.missing: The shot of a bow, a crossbow or a thrown weapon (ranged combat); a Shield effect on the player does not soften the blows that land on it; the resistance to normal weapons is not yet proven with a skilled character in game; the chance to hit is not yet compared with the formula in play, a blow that lands on health with the opponent's bar is not yet seen, and the fights between characters and the guards joining them are not yet seen.

features.name: Death and bodies
features.what: Actors die, the player's death is handled, and bodies are opened and looted through the container strip.
features.proof: tests/aga_player_dead_test.c, tests/aga_levelled_contents_test.c; CORPSE-LOOT-60 gated in v0.0.60-dev3.

features.name: Crime and the law
features.what: Theft, attacks and trespass seen by witnesses raise a bounty; guards arrest, fine or jail.
features.proof: tests/aga_crime_rules_test.c, tests/test_crime.py (theft, assault, murder and an owned bed: the witnesses, the bounty by the game settings, the crime message, every witness's disposition change, pursuit or attack; the fine, jail and the prison markers; OnMurder, PayFine, PayFineThief, GotoJail and the guards' Alarmed); since v0.0.62.
features.missing: Pickpocketing (no pickpocket window yet) and picking an owned lock (no lockpicks yet) have their rules but no event in the game; the arrest, the fine and jail, and the guards that come after a theft in view of them (the witnessed theft in the census office), are checked by tests and not yet seen in play; the pursuers and the Alarmed marks are not kept in saved games.

features.name: Sneaking and stealing
features.what: Sneaking (the slower walk, its fatigue cost, never running) and the awareness check that decides whether the witnesses of a theft notice the sneaking thief; the theft itself raises the crime. Sneak and Security rise in jail.
features.reference: OpenMW 0.51 sneak and security; UESP Morrowind:Sneak, Morrowind:Security
features.proof: tests/aga_move_rules_test.c, tests/aga_crime_rules_test.c; docs/GAME_FORMULAS.md (crime, sneaking, locks and detection).
features.missing: Pickpocketing, lockpicking and trap disarming (no pickpocket window, lockpicks or probes yet), the sneak indicator, and detection by the beings that walk past a sneaking player.

features.name: Spell effects
features.what: Magic effects applied to actors over their duration, the active effects display, and the effect rules.
features.reference: OpenMW 0.51 magic effects; UESP Morrowind:Magic Effects
features.missing: Resistances from abilities, reflection, the movement effects, the caster's half of Absorb, and some effects that other systems must read (Shield does not yet soften blows); an ended Fortify Attribute leaves a drop counted as damage.

features.name: Player casting
features.what: Ready a spell, pay the magicka, roll to succeed, deliver Self, Touch and Target effects; the starting spells of race, birth sign and class; enchanted items that cast (Cast When Strikes, Cast When Used, Constant Effect, scrolls).
features.proof: tests/test_mwscript.py CastRuleTests and EffectTests, docs/MAGIC_EFFECTS.md (Casting, Enchanted items); the four kinds of enchanted item seen in game on the v0.0.61-dev2 image with the dev3 engine.
features.missing: The hands' casting gesture; the worn Constant Effect items of non-player characters; an enchanted blow of a non-player character on the player is not yet seen in game, and its charge is kept for the session only; Tribunal and Bloodmoon items are not in the item table.

features.name: Spellmaking
features.what: Making spells at a spellmaker: the player names the spell, adds effects with magnitude, duration, area and range, sees the point cost and the price, and buys it into his made spells (64 at most, saved).
features.missing: The spell's success chance is not shown; the window is checked by tests and not yet seen in play.

features.name: Alchemy
features.what: Making potions from apparatus and ingredients in the alchemy window (apparatus quality, the effects the Alchemy skill reveals, strength and duration from skill, Intelligence, Luck and apparatus, success roll, skill gain); drinking potions; eating an ingredient for its first effect.
features.missing: Several potions at once and a typed potion name; ingredient and apparatus pictures in the window; non-player characters do not drink potions.

features.name: Enchanting
features.what: Enchanting items with soul gems at an enchanter: the player names the item, picks a thing that can take an enchantment and a filled soul gem, adds effects within the item's capacity, and buys the enchanted item (64 at most, saved). Items that are already enchanted cast; see Player casting.
features.missing: Ranged and thrown weapons cannot be enchanted (the item catalogue holds melee weapons only), soul trapping and recharging are not in, and the window is checked by tests and not yet seen in play.

features.name: Inventory
features.what: The inventory window with the item list, the preview that follows worn clothes and armour at once, the armour rating, the equip rules including enchanted weapons and shields; drop and pick up (a drop in a tomb with an uneven floor was seen to work on v0.0.63-dev3).
features.missing: The armour rating adds a Shield effect that the blows do not yet use; the inventory picture does not show a held light.

features.name: Carry weight
features.what: The weight carried against Strength times fEncumbranceStrMult: slower with more load, no movement over the limit with the game's line, the burden bar in the inventory; no limit on the number of kinds of item.
features.reference: OpenMW 0.51 encumbrance (mwclass/actor.cpp, mwclass/npc.cpp, mwgui/inventorywindow.cpp, mwgui/windowmanagerimp.cpp); UESP Morrowind:Strength
features.missing: Burden and Feather magnitudes from the spell effects (the call is in), and the in-game check on a numbered build.

features.name: Containers
features.what: Baskets, crates, barrels and chests open into a strip of their items to take or put back, with levelled contents rolled by the original's rules; the strip opens in about 80 ms with hundreds of kinds carried.
features.missing: The container window's in-game check and the per-area tables for container data.

features.name: Barter
features.what: Buying and selling with prices from disposition and Mercantile: two plain pages, Buy (the merchant's stock) and Sell (the player's things), one thing a click at the game's offer, only the kinds the merchant's service flags trade.
features.missing: The original's trade window: an offer the player changes, a running total of both sides, the merchant's gold limit and restocking, haggling; the goods are not shown as item icons; a merchant keeps only 12 item changes.

features.name: Training
features.what: Paid training in the dialogue window.
features.missing: A trained skill does not yet count toward the level.

features.name: Dialogue
features.what: The conversation window, topics, conditions, disposition, persuasion and services; all 7,411 dialogue result scripts run; the headline of its own tracker is shown below.
features.missing: The rows of docs/DIALOGUE_FEATURES.md that are not done.

features.name: Voices
features.what: Character voice lines and creature sounds mapped into the world and heard in game.
features.reference: the original's voice files; OpenMW 0.51 sound handling
features.missing: Rows of the voice tracker not yet heard in game.

features.name: Journal and quests
features.what: The journal with dated entries and the quest book; journal indexes kept by the dialogue and the scripts. Dates read as in the original (18 Last Seed, Day 3) in the journal, the rest window and the saved game list. Each quest's outcome: the entry of the ending reached, and the quest under the finished ones once an ending's entry finishes it (success and failure endings alike); a restart entry reopens it.
features.missing: Topic names in quest entries are not links yet; quests run only as far as the scripts do.

features.name: Factions and ranks
features.what: Faction membership, rank and reputation read by the dialogue conditions and the scripts; the guild masters' advancement check (the next rank's attribute, skill and reputation needs); faction reactions in disposition; expulsion for a reported crime against a member or a faction's item, with the original message, and reinstatement by the dialogue's results.
features.proof: docs/DIALOGUE_FEATURES.md (rank requirement conditions live); tests/test_dialogue_lut.py; tests/test_crime.py; tests/test_combat_settings_text.py; tests/aga_statswin_test.c.
features.missing: Not yet walked through in game (the stats page's factions, ranks, next rank's needs, reputation and bounty are new in v0.0.64-dev3).

features.name: MWScript compiler
features.what: All 1,207 scripts of the three masters compile to the compact bytecode, with the original's quirks kept.
features.reference: OpenMW 0.51 script compiler (behaviour only); UESP Morrowind:Scripting
features.proof: tests/test_mwscript.py; docs/MWSCRIPT_BYTECODE.md (1,207 of 1,207 compiled, none refused).

features.name: MWScript functions
features.what: The compiler knows 504 functions and instructions; the interpreter and the host carry out 460 of them (v0.0.62: the player's control switches, the small functions such as Move, MoveWorld, SetPos, Face and GetLOS, the placing family PlaceAtPC, PlaceAtMe, PlaceItem and PlaceItemCell, the fades, the forced sneak, the resistances and the crimes; v0.0.63: the moons, HasItemEquipped, the forced run, ExplodeSpell, the werewolf set, the scale functions, the water breathing functions, the effect family Chameleon to DefendBonus, the game hour and moon phases, the view switches, the armour type, SameFaction, RemoveEffects, the soul gems, and the console group callable from scripts: Show, ShowVars, ToggleAI, ResetActors, OutputRefInfo and the console aliases), the rest compile to the not-yet call. The game's scripts use 251 distinct functions.
features.reference: OpenMW 0.51 script extensions (behaviour); UESP Morrowind:Script Functions
features.proof: tools/mwscript/functions.py (the table and its RUN and HOST sets); tests/test_mwscript.py; tests/aga_controls_test.c; tests/aga_move_rules_test.c; tests/aga_crime_rules_test.c.
features.missing: 44 table functions are not carried out, each with its reason on the console commands page (the drawing switches, the path grid, the fog of war, the water level, the wind, the vision bonus, the levelled list edits, the skipped animation). How many of the 251 used ones are among them is pending a measurement run; the 28 scripts that lack a function all belong to Mournhold and Solstheim.

features.name: Scripts that run whole
features.what: 605 of the 1,074 scripts the original uses run as scripts and 9 more are carried by the game's own code (the character creation scripts, compared step by step with it, and Main). Every Vvardenfell script the original uses runs: of Morrowind.esm's 616 scripts, 518 run, 9 are carried, 1 is only in an add-on world and 88 are not used (nothing in the original names or starts them). All 7,411 dialogue result scripts run.
features.reference: the original scripts run under OpenMW 0.51
features.proof: docs/MWSCRIPT_FEATURES.md and docs/mwscript-features.json (measured 9 November 2026, v0.0.63); tests/test_mwscript.py.
features.missing: The scripts of the expansions wait for their worlds: Tribunal.esm's 255 scripts are 42 run in Vvardenfell, 8 lacking a function, 186 waiting for Mournhold and 19 named by nothing; Bloodmoon.esm's 336 are 45 run, 20 lacking a function, 245 waiting for Solstheim and 26 named by nothing. The census tray smoke test is not run.

features.name: Music
features.what: The soundtrack by region and situation, playing through loads.
features.reference: OpenMW 0.51 music handling; the original's soundtrack

features.name: Sound effects
features.what: Door, footstep, ambient and spell sounds from the sound records.
features.missing: Area sounds from the markers, and the creature and combat sounds that are not yet mapped.

features.name: HUD and messages
features.what: The health, magicka and fatigue bars, the crosshair and aim box, the message line and message boxes, the active effects. Since v0.0.63 a breath bar under water, the opponent's health bar, and the box of a spoken line in type 2 (the default, drawn at once, blackening nothing outside the box, so the bars under the view stay visible; type 1, the rising strip, is a choice in Options).
features.missing: The breath bar, the opponent's health bar and the type 2 text box are checked by tests and not yet seen in play.

features.name: Menus and options
features.what: The front menu, options, key bindings and the console. Since v0.0.63 the console carries the original game's console commands with their short aliases and the stat family on any reference, takes up to 1,000 commands, and the options Always use best attack and Text box type are one saved value shared with the console.
features.proof: tests/aga_menu_test.c, tests/aga_keymap_test.c, tests/aga_console_test.c, docs/CONSOLE_COMMANDS_MORROWIND.md (every command and its reason when it is not carried out).
features.missing: A performance and quality preset and a screen-mode choice; new defaults do not reach existing settings files; the console's earlier-command keys are not yet checked in play.

features.name: The in-game map
features.what: A world map and a local map.
features.missing: The original-style map with explored areas, the local map and the landmark markers.
